   - `:state {:status :absent ...}`

   Source acceptance does not establish deployment or a post-change production close. “Observation exercises exist” is too easy to misread as acquired observations. State instead: “Rubric and validator mechanisms exist; zero qualifying annotations and zero licensed state/outcome pairs exist.”

3. **F04’s remaining obligation needs prospective acquisition controls.** Add: independently authorized observer origin, distinct exact-subject review, predeclared close eligibility/sampling, observer blinding from posterior and close disposition, immutable pre-cutoff evidence admission, and retention of insufficient/ambiguous/conflicting observations. Otherwise choosing successful closes after outcome reveal can bias A even if each annotation validates.

After settlement, require actual matched Q/C scorer consumption and evidence. Do not make “state-dependent disposition bridge” an already-adopted completion requirement unless the owner ratifies it.

No `:machine-q-enabled?` production interface exists in the inspected tree. This is stronger and more precise than simply saying real inputs must feed the scorer.

6. **E02 should credit close-retention only at source scope.** The contract/writer/runner were accepted at ledger `3a6f4f61`, but no post-change production close or serving-code identity proves the new source ran. Retain the remaining model threading and evidence-manifest acquisition explicitly.

Missing obligation: the first measured-A annotation workflow itself—strict admitted-evidence resolver, authority records, one predeclared real close, blinded observation, exact-subject acceptance, then close/annotation pairing—should appear under F04/E02. One annotation still does not establish seven-row coverage or measured A.
